le_chatelier_pressure.about: Squeeze N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3: fewer moles of gas on the right, so the equilibrium moves right and more red NH3 particles appear while the gauge rises.
le_chatelier_pressure.hint: Use the default particle_lab reaction; set vol to a falling expression. Say 'shifts toward fewer moles of gas'.

le_chatelier_expand.about: Let the same gas expand: the equilibrium moves left toward more moles of gas, so NH3 particles turn into N2 and H2.
le_chatelier_expand.hint: vol rises above 1; the plunger moves up.

le_chatelier_concentration.about: Add N2 at about 3 s: the system consumes it, shifting right (more NH3).
le_chatelier_concentration.hint: dA adds particles of species A (negative removes them).

le_chatelier_temperature_exothermic.about: Heat N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3 (exothermic, dH = -92 kJ/mol) from 400 K to 520 K: K falls, the equilibrium moves left, NH3 particles decrease, and all particles move faster.
le_chatelier_temperature_exothermic.hint: Kt uses vanthoff with the reaction's dH; spd speeds the particle clock while heating. For an endothermic reaction use a positive dH.

equal_moles_no_shift.about: H2 + I2 <=> 2HI has the same number of gas moles on both sides: squeezing raises the pressure but does not shift the equilibrium.
equal_moles_no_shift.hint: Colours: H2 white, I2 purple, HI orange.

dissociation.about: N2O4 <=> 2NO2 (colourless to brown): compressing favours N2O4 (fewer moles), expanding favours NO2.
dissociation.hint: A = N2O4, C = NO2 (b = 0 and d = 0 mean absent).

boyle_law.about: Pure gas, no reaction: the same particles in a smaller volume hit the walls more often, so the gauge (pressure) rises as the plunger falls (P is proportional to 1/V).
boyle_law.hint: Give all four stoichiometric numbers as 0 so no reaction happens; only nA is used.
